name: Chisel
text: Adopt the **automated daily triage of the top 10 unique false negatives**, with Engineering owning the retrain threshold (precision <90%). This balances speed and scale—Legal reviews only the worst systemic harms, while Engineering validates patterns and prevents noise drowning. The trade-off is accepting a 24-hour delay for emergent slurs, but it’s the only option that scales without burning out Legal or missing the forest for the trees.

name: Sift
text: The "slur mutation tracker" assumes we can predict every new slur variant—false. Slurs mutate unpredictably; the tracker will miss edge cases until they explode. Instead, mandate **Engineering to build a real-time anomaly detector** (not a tracker) that flags *any* sudden spike in flagged content, with Legal reviewing only the top 5 *confirmed* harms daily. Settle it by running a 7-day pilot comparing false negatives before and after.

name: Scope
text: Adopt the **automated daily triage of the top 10 unique false negatives**, with Engineering owning the retrain threshold (precision <90%). This balances speed and scale—Legal reviews only the worst systemic harms, while Engineering validates patterns and prevents noise drowning. The trade-off is accepting a slight delay (24 hours) in catching emergent slurs, but it avoids overreacting to noise and ensures consistent, measurable improvements.

name: Scriv
text: The "slur mutation tracker" shifts the burden to Engineering to predict the unpredictable—new slurs emerge faster than we can model them. Instead, mandate **a hybrid system**: Engineering builds a lightweight real-time anomaly detector (flags spikes in novel terms), while Legal reviews the top 5 *confirmed* false negatives *hourly* during peak spikes. Settle it with a 3-day pilot comparing harm reduction vs. false positives.
